cohort: 40 term pregnant women with a previous one lower segment caesarean section (LSCS) and an unfavourable cervix were randomly assigned to either the intracervical Foley catheter or vaginal IMN group.
finding: Intracervical Foley catheter resulted in a significantly shorter induction to delivery interval (22.2+/-4.99hr) compared to vaginal IMN (26.1+/-3.98 hr) and was found to be effective, safe, and acceptable for labor induction, albeit with more maternal pyrexia.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery and the rate of failed induction were not significantly different between the intracervical Foley catheter and vaginal IMN groups.
